prompt.eta:
Select the nearest existing duration for wall-clock time from the visible prefix to the final verifier result; preserve all options, including the 1-minute minimum and 1-year maximum. Estimate time separately from future batch count: already-issued work and verification can consume time with zero new batches.
Use timestamps, recent action cadence, call status, observed waits, and remaining operational stages. For nonterminal direct interaction, include likely sequential preparation, data entry, evidence checks, and submission or finalization where supported by the goal and schema. Do not assign the shortest duration merely because one milestone succeeded or much text has already been produced. Researching unresolved prerequisites is not equivalent to being ready to submit.
For delegation, estimate the remaining critical path of pending work plus supported parent synthesis/delivery and verifier latency; never sum parallel child runtimes or infer hours from the size of the delegated prompt. A large research assignment may return quickly. Use observed latency of comparable visible operations when available, without multiplying by a universal per-call constant.
For issued terminal finalization without rejection or continuation evidence, estimate only residual verifier latency, not the ideal unfinished task. A finished terminal observation can have zero time remaining; select the minimum available duration when the true residual is below it. Missing or IN_PROGRESS completion feedback alone does not justify a long delay. In an explicitly continuing staged workflow, include supported downstream execution instead.
Observed long waits matter, but elapsed time is not automatically remaining time and a past wait need not repeat. Do not invent unseen future waits from task complexity or authorization requirements; their duration is inherently uncertain.
prompt.progress:
Select the existing remaining-batch option using this evidence order:
1. Inspect the latest finalization call and feedback first. An issued attempt_completion, attempt_completion_with_result, equivalent finalization, or terminal stop supports exactly zero future batches, including when its response is missing, empty, or IN_PROGRESS. Do not substitute a small positive remainder. Incomplete goals, elaborate plans, and missing schema fields alone do not override terminal evidence; actual trajectories can end imperfectly.
2. Override that terminal interpretation only with visible rejection, validation failure, instructions to continue, or explicit workflow evidence that this completion closes a phase and execution remains. A plan listing future tasks is not by itself proof those tasks will be issued after completion. Conversely, FINISHED on an ordinary tool or send_message_to_user is not trajectory finalization. Estimate supported recovery, phase continuation, and resubmission rather than automatically adding one retry.
3. For nonterminal prefixes, compare the goal and required output schema with evidence already obtained. Identify remaining operational stages: missing facts or prerequisites, direct actions, state/evidence checks, synthesis or artifact delivery, and finalization. Treat schema fields as evidence requirements, not one tool call per field. Distinguish information that can be composed from existing evidence from information requiring another external action. Include required verification when likely to be issued, but do not invent audits or perfect-result repairs.
4. In direct browser work, assess whether the agent is still researching prerequisites, preparing controls, entering data, or verifying an outcome. Approval/readiness is not completion of preparation. Explicit field-entry instructions and alternating action/read patterns support multiple sequential batches. A long form with unresolved facts, essays, or submission evidence can remain early even after many calls. A prohibition on submission removes the purchase/submission stage, not all preparation and evidence gathering. Respect terminal evidence even if preparation is imperfect.
5. In delegated workflows, map remaining stages to the current agent only. One delegation can supply many facts or outputs. A returned report may still require supported synthesis, delivery, phase transitions, and finalization; a complete-looking user message is not a completion tool. Do not collapse such continuation to a fractional near-zero remainder or count child searches as parent calls.
6. At empty or early history, distinguish direct interaction, delegation, research, and planning roles. Goal length and schema size do not impose a minimum trajectory; a planning or research agent may finalize early. Use observed execution mode and action granularity, not a universal workflow. Choose the best-supported existing option without arbitrary constants or forced monotonicity.
prompt.scope: Classify actual future tool-call batches issued by the current agent using only the visible history and existing options. Calls issued together count as one batch. A spawn or for_each may cover a large task in one parent batch; child internal calls do not count as parent batches. Tool responses, waits, and continued execution of an issued call add no batches. Predict likely actual continuation, not the work an ideal agent would perform.
